thread.title: Pittsburgh man pleads guilty to firearm possession as a convicted felon
thread.title_full: Pittsburgh man pleads guilty to firearm possession as a convicted felon

author: Keystone Today
title: Pittsburgh man pleads guilty to firearm possession as a convicted felon
text:
Chaz Mitchell, a 36-year-old resident of the Homewood neighborhood in Pittsburgh, pleaded guilty on May 12 to possession of a firearm and ammunition by a convicted felon, according to United States Attorney Troy Rivetti.
Mitchell entered his plea before United States District Judge J. Nicholas Ranjan. The case highlights ongoing efforts by law enforcement agencies to address gun violence and enforce federal firearms laws among individuals with prior felony convictions.
According to information presented in court, officers from the Pittsburgh Bureau of Police observed Mitchell with an assault rifle and sawed-off shotgun on July 5, 2025, while attempting to execute a state arrest warrant for unrelated charges. Mitchell initially refused to exit the residence until the SWAT unit arrived. After his surrender and arrest, police executed a search warrant at the residence and recovered an assault rifle, sawed-off shotgun, pistol, and ammunition. Federal law prohibits anyone previously convicted of felony state firearms offenses from possessing firearms or ammunition.
Judge Ranjan scheduled sentencing for August 21. Mitchell faces up to 15 years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000 under federal statutes; however, actual sentencing will depend on federal guidelines considering both the seriousness of the offense and his prior criminal history.
Assistant United States Attorney V. Joseph Sonson is prosecuting the case. The investigation was conducted by the Pittsburgh Bureau of Police along with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.
This prosecution falls under Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), which brings together law enforcement agencies at all levels with communities aiming to reduce violent crime and gun violence. The Department launched an updated violent crime reduction strategy for PSN in May 2021 that focuses on fostering community trust and legitimacy; supporting organizations that help prevent violence; setting strategic enforcement priorities; and measuring results.
